evidence.section: 2.3. Strengthening Mechanisms and Cryogenic Deformation Behavior
evidence.quote: The prevalence of twins at 4.2 K results from a combination of reduced SFE, increased flow stress, and the predominance of edge dislocations.
The L12 nano-precipitates also modify dislocation configuration and the propensity for forming different sessile barriers
These microstructural modifications not only increase strength but also elevate the effective stress, promote the formation of Hirth locks, and prevent catastrophic dislocation avalanches.

The strength enhancement originates from the concurrent contributions of increased Peierls stress (σTh) due to severe lattice distortion and precipitation strengthening (σAth) from ultrafine L12 precipitates.

mechanisms.name: solid-solution strengthening by lattice distortion (increased Peierls stress)

mechanisms.name: Hirth lock formation by partial dislocation interaction

evidence.quote: the synergistic eﬀects of high lattice distortion and L12 precipitates-dislocation interactions promote both enhanced eﬀective stress and Hirth lock formation, providing a robust mechanism for suppressing DPF and enhancing cryogenic mechanical stability.
